newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania on track for NATO admission - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: Romania on track for NATO admission - U.S. official.

text.p: A senior U.S. defence official said on Thursday Romania's chances of early admission into NATO had been significantly boosted by recent democratic elections and improved ties with neighbours.
"Romania is clearly on the right road on its course to join the alliance," U.S. Defence Under-Secretary for Policy Walter Slocombe told a news conference.
Slocombe, on a 24-hour visit to Bucharest, had talks with senior Romanian defence officials to review the country's military reform efforts to join the Western defence umbrella.

He praised the "peaceful transfer of power" following presidential and general elections last November, when centrists threw leftwingers from office for the first time since the 1989 collapse of communism.
"This confirms that democracy has taken firm roots in Romania. That fact is an important plus in Romania's bid for early admission to NATO," he said.
In 1993 Romania was the first ex-communist East European country to sign up for NATO's Partnership for Peace scheme of boosting military ties with former Cold War foes.

The new centrist ruling coalition is seeking to improve the country's chances of gaining early membership of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation along with Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, so far seen as favourite first-wave candidates.

"We commend Romania for progress made in building good relations with neighbours," Slocombe said of a treaty signed with Hungary last year settling old rifts over borders and ethnic minorities. He also singled out treaty talks with Ukraine, due to resume in Bucharest next week.
NATO would decide on who joins the alliance's eastward expansion drive at its Madrid summit in July, Slocombe said.

Apparently leaving the door open for Bucharest's hopes of early admission, he said "a decision has not been taken and will not be taken for some time" regarding which candidates the United States would support.
